why: ADOPTED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 P2), was `declined`/`absent`. The constraint the prior row states still holds -- a node's entities live in the arena of the executor that CREATED it and registration is one-way -- but it forbids MOVING a node, not NAMING the attachment. `rclcpp::Executor::add_node(node, notify = true)` (any pointer-like to a node, rclcpp's `Node::SharedPtr` included) and `executors::SingleThreadedExecutor::add_node` CHECK the attachment construction already made: an own node is a no-op; an uninitialised node or one created on another executor aborts naming it, with `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_FOREIGN_NODE`, because spinning this executor would never reach its callbacks. `notify` is accepted and ignored. ENVELOPE: what a user loses is still handing a built node to a different executor. Held by `executor_node_members_runtime.cpp`. PRIOR ROW: an rclcpp node is standalone and is ATTACHED to an executor, which is what makes it movable between executors and spinnable by more than one. static entity storage: the executor's entity table is an arena sized at compile time (`NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_HANDLES`) with no allocator behind it, and a `HandleId` is an index into it. Registration is one-way -- no slot is ever reclaimed and no handle is ever invalidated. A node's entities are allocated in the arena of the executor that created it (`cpp:Executor::create_node`), so attachment is not a separate step and cannot be undone. What a user loses: handing an already-built node to a different executor.
